# DarkSlide v1.2.0

DarkSlide 1.2.0 adds 3D LUT interchange in the `.cube` format. You can bring a conversion LUT into DarkSlide as a custom preset, and take any preset back out as a `.cube` file that other applications can apply.

## Highlights

- Import a `.cube` LUT as a custom preset — through the Import button, the file picker, or by dropping the file on the Custom tab.
- An imported LUT performs the negative→positive conversion **in place of** DarkSlide's density inversion and film-base compensation. Every parametric adjustment — exposure, contrast, temperature/tint, black and white point, highlight protection, saturation, curves — still applies on top of the LUT's output.
- Imported LUT presets start with neutral sliders, so the LUT reproduces the look it was authored for rather than being layered under DarkSlide's usual defaults.
- Export any preset as a 33×33×33 `.cube` LUT that bakes the full conversion: inversion, film-base compensation, colour matrix, lab style, and all tonal stages. The result converts a raw negative scan to a finished positive in Resolve, Premiere, or any other host that reads `.cube`.
- LUTs run on both the WebGPU and CPU preview paths with matching trilinear interpolation, so previews, tiled renders, exports, batch runs, and contact sheets all agree.
- Auto white balance and dust detection see the same LUT-converted image the renderer does.
- A LUT that does not invert is flagged at import, since DarkSlide runs it where its own inversion would go.

## Why This Matters

Film scanning workflows already trade LUTs. Being able to load one directly means a conversion someone else authored can be used as-is, then refined with DarkSlide's sliders instead of being approximated by them. Baking in the other direction lets a preset developed here travel to a video or stills workflow that has no notion of DarkSlide's pipeline.

## Format Notes

- 3D LUTs only (`LUT_3D_SIZE`). 1D LUTs are rejected with an explanation rather than upsampled. Sizes from 2 to 129 are accepted.
- `TITLE`, `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX`, comments, and CRLF line endings are all handled. The title becomes the preset name when present.
- A LUT is treated as operating in DarkSlide's working space; a colour space named in the file's comments is not honoured.
- Geometry (crop, rotation, level angle) and the spatial filters (sharpen, noise reduction, dust removal) are excluded from a baked LUT — they are not per-pixel colour operations.
- Baking uses the values a preset stores. The measurements DarkSlide normally takes per frame — estimated film base, flare floor, residual base offset, highlight density — are baked neutral.
- LUT payloads are held in IndexedDB, which stores the table natively. The localStorage mirror omits them; if IndexedDB is unavailable, a LUT preset will keep its settings but lose its table.

## Desktop Downloads

GitHub Actions builds and attaches installers for each supported desktop platform:

- macOS: universal Apple Silicon and Intel `.dmg`
- Windows: `.msi` and NSIS `.exe`
- Linux: `.deb` and `.AppImage`

## Known Notes

- macOS builds are not notarized. On first launch, macOS may require opening the app through System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
- Windows and Linux builds are unsigned.
- RAW support is available in the desktop app and remains an advanced workflow; JPEG, PNG, TIFF, and WebP are the stable browser-supported formats.

## Checks

This release adds coverage for `.cube` parsing (including axis ordering, malformed tables, 1D rejection, and a real-world 35³ file), trilinear sampling, the JSON transport used by `.darkslide` files, LUT-versus-inversion behaviour in the render pipeline, bake fidelity against the per-pixel path, import → export round-tripping, and the preset pane's import and export actions. GitHub Actions builds the desktop installers on macOS, Windows, and Linux and retains them as workflow artifacts.
